defining property `A([D]) = -[ker q]` for an arbitrary family. Before this file that
equation had **no instantiation**: `DivFamily` had no producer, so no value of the Abel
map was ever computed, and "the Abel map sends divisors to their line bundles" was a
statement about an empty domain.

## What is proved

`abelMap_zero`: `A([∅]) = 0`, i.e. the empty divisor goes to the **identity** of the
relative Picard group. Kleiman §3: `O(∅) = O`, so this is the normalisation an Abel map
must satisfy, and it is the first computed value of `abelMap` in the project.

The proof is where the empty divisor's arithmetic shows up. `ker (0 : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0)` is

298	theorem Module.Flat.of_subsingleton' {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type u}
299	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Subsingleton M] : Module.Flat R M :=
300	  Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv
301	    (({ toFun := fun _ => PUnit.unit, invFun := fun _ => 0,
302	        left_inv := fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _, right_inv := fun _ => rfl,
303	        map_add' := fun _ _ => rfl,
304	        map_smul' := fun _ _ => rfl } : M ≃ₗ[R] PUnit.{u+1}))
305	
306	namespace Scheme.Modules
307	
308	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}}
309	
310	/-- **The sections of a zero sheaf of modules over any open form a subsingleton.**
311	
312	`Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf` is additive, so it carries `M` to a zero presheaf of
313	abelian groups, whose value at `V` is a zero object of `Ab` and hence a
314	subsingleton. -/
315	theorem subsingleton_sections_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M)
316	    (V : Y.Opens) : Subsingleton Γ(M, V) :=
317	  AddCommGrpCat.subsingleton_of_isZero
318	    ((Functor.map_isZero (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf Y) hM).obj _)
319	
320	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules is flat over any base morphism**, with no hypothesis on
321	the morphism at all.
322	
323	`CoherentSheafFlat` asks each section module `Γ(M, V)` to be flat over `Γ(S, U)`. The
324	section modules are subsingletons (`subsingleton_sections_of_isZero`), and a
325	subsingleton module is flat. -/
326	theorem coherentSheafFlat_of_isZero {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ S') {M : Y.Modules}
327	    (hM : IsZero M) : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat g M := by
328	  intro U _ V _ e
329	  letI : Module Γ(S', U) Γ(M, V) := Module.compHom _ (g.appLE U V e).hom
330	  haveI := subsingleton_sections_of_isZero hM V
331	  exact Module.Flat.of_subsingleton'
332	
333	/-- **The annihilator ideal sheaf of a zero sheaf of modules is `⊤`.**
334	
335	Each affine-local annihilator is the whole ring (`Module.annihilator_eq_top_iff` at a
336	subsingleton module), and `ofIdeals` of the constant-`⊤` family is `⊤` because `⊤` is
337	itself an ideal sheaf below it. -/
338	theorem annihilator_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
339	    Scheme.Modules.annihilator M = ⊤ :=
340	  top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup (by
341	    intro U
342	    haveI := subsingleton_sections_of_isZero hM U.1
343	    exact le_of_eq (Module.annihilator_eq_top_iff.mpr inferInstance).symm))
344	
345	/-- **The schematic support of a zero sheaf of modules is empty.**
346	
347	Its annihilator is `⊤`, and the subscheme cut out by the unit ideal sheaf has empty
348	carrier. -/
349	theorem isEmpty_schematicSupport_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
350	    IsEmpty (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupport M) := by
351	  rw [Scheme.Modules.schematicSupport, annihilator_of_isZero hM]
352	  infer_instance
353	
354	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules has proper support over any base**, unconditionally.
355	
356	The support is empty, and a morphism out of an empty scheme is finite, hence proper.
357	This is the field of `DivFamily` that is a *real* hypothesis for a nonempty divisor —
358	properness of `D → T` — and it is free for the empty one, with **no** properness
359	assumption on the ambient morphism. -/
360	theorem hasProperSupport_of_isZero {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ S') {M : Y.Modules}
361	    (hM : IsZero M) : Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport g M := by
362	  haveI := isEmpty_schematicSupport_of_isZero hM
363	  exact IsProper.instOfIsFinite _
364	
365	end Scheme.Modules
366	
367	/-! ## §3. The empty divisor -/
368	
369	namespace Scheme
370	
371	variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ S) (T : Over S)
372	
373	/-- **The structure sheaf is locally trivial of rank one.**
374	
375	`RelPicFunctor.isLocallyTrivial_unit` is `private`, so it is restated here rather
376	than reused: on any affine open the identity is the required trivialisation. -/
377	theorem isLocallyTrivial_unit' {Y : Scheme.{u}} :
378	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf) := by
379	  intro x
380	  obtain ⟨W, hW_aff, hxW, -⟩ :=
381	    exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (X := Y) (x := x) (U := ⊤)
382	      (show x ∈ (⊤ : Y.Opens) from trivial)
383	  exact ⟨W, hxW, hW_aff,
384	    ⟨(Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback W.ι).app _ ≪≫ Modules.pullbackUnitIso W.ι⟩⟩
385	
386	/-- **THE EMPTY DIVISOR**, and with it the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily` for
387	any `π : X ⟶ S` and any test object `T`.
388	
389	`F = 0`, `q = 0`. The kernel ideal is then all of `O_{X_T}` — via
390	`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`, since the source of `q` is the pulled-back unit — which
391	is invertible, so the *divisor condition* holds for the geometric reason it should:
392	`O_{X_T}/O_{X_T} = 0` cuts out `D = ∅`, an effective relative divisor.
393	
394	No hypothesis on `π`: not proper, not smooth, not even separated. Compare the general
395	case, where `properSupport` and `flat` are substantive conditions. -/
396	noncomputable def DivFamily.zero : DivFamily π T where
397	  F := 0
398	  isFinitePresentation := Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_isZero (isZero_zero _)
399	  flat := Modules.coherentSheafFlat_of_isZero _ (isZero_zero _)
400	  properSupport := Modules.hasProperSupport_of_isZero _ (isZero_zero _)
401	  q := 0
402	  epi := (isZero_zero _).epi _
403	  kerLocallyTrivial :=
404	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.of_iso
405	      (Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource (X := (Scheme.Modules.pullback
406	        (Limits.pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))
407	        (Y := (0 : (Limits.pullback π T.hom).Modules))).symm
408	      (LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.of_iso
409	        (Modules.pullbackUnitIso (Limits.pullback.fst π T.hom)).symm
410	        isLocallyTrivial_unit')
411	
412	instance DivFamily.instNonempty : Nonempty (DivFamily π T) :=
413	  ⟨DivFamily.zero π T⟩
414	
415	/-! ## §4. Base change, fibre degree, and the degree-zero slice
416	
417	The empty divisor is not just a fibrewise accident: base change carries it to the
418	empty divisor of the new test object, so its classes assemble into a **global section**
419	of `DivFunctor`, and its fibre degree is `0` at every point of every base. -/
420	
421	/-- **The pulled-back empty divisor is the empty divisor**, up to the divisor
422	equivalence — both `F`-sheaves are zero and any two morphisms into a zero object
423	agree.
424	
425	This is what makes `zeroClass` below a genuine global section of `DivFunctor` rather
426	than an unrelated choice at each test object. -/
427	theorem DivFamily.pullbackAlong_zero {T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
428	    ((DivFamily.zero π T).pullbackAlong ψ).Rel (DivFamily.zero π T') :=
429	  ⟨(Functor.map_isZero (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ))
430	      (isZero_zero _)).iso (isZero_zero _),
431	    (isZero_zero _).eq_of_tgt _ _⟩
432	
433	/-- **The fibre of the empty divisor is zero** — `fiberModule` is a module pullback,
434	which is additive. -/
435	theorem DivFamily.isZero_fiberModule_zero (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
436	    IsZero ((Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t (DivFamily.zero π T).F) :=
437	  Functor.map_isZero _ (isZero_zero _)
438	
439	/-- **The empty divisor has fibre degree `0`**, at every point of every base.
440	
441	`deg ∅ = dim_{κ(t)} Γ(∅, O_∅) = 0`: the fibre is the zero module, its global sections
442	are a subsingleton, and `finrank` of a subsingleton is `0`. -/
443	theorem DivFamily.fiberDeg_zero (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
444	    (DivFamily.zero π T).fiberDeg t = 0 := by
445	  letI := (Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t
446	    ((Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t (DivFamily.zero π T).F)
447	  haveI : Subsingleton
448	      Γ((Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t (DivFamily.zero π T).F, ⊤) :=
449	    Modules.subsingleton_sections_of_isZero (DivFamily.isZero_fiberModule_zero π T t) _
450	  exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton
451	
452	/-- **The empty divisor has constant fibre degree `0`** — `HasFiberDeg zero 0`, the
453	predicate the degree-`d` subfunctor `DivFunctorDeg` is cut out by. -/
454	theorem DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_zero : (DivFamily.zero π T).HasFiberDeg 0 :=
455	  fun t => DivFamily.fiberDeg_zero π T t
456	
457	/-- **The class of the empty divisor** in `Div_{X/S}(T)`: the first inhabitant of the
458	relative-divisor functor's value at any test object. -/
459	noncomputable def DivFunctor.zeroClass : (DivFunctor π).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
460	  Quotient.mk _ (DivFamily.zero π T)
461	
462	instance DivFunctor.instNonemptyObj : Nonempty ((DivFunctor π).obj (Opposite.op T)) :=
463	  ⟨DivFunctor.zeroClass π T⟩
464	
465	/-- **`DivFunctor` carries the zero class to the zero class**, i.e. `zeroClass` is a
466	*global section* of `Div_{X/S}` — a compatible family over all test objects, not a
467	choice per object. -/
468	theorem DivFunctor.map_zeroClass {T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
469	    (DivFunctor π).map ψ.op (DivFunctor.zeroClass π T) = DivFunctor.zeroClass π T' :=
470	  Quotient.sound (DivFamily.pullbackAlong_zero π T ψ)
471	
472	/-- **The empty divisor's class has degree `0`**, in the class-level predicate the
473	degree slices use. -/
474	theorem DivFunctor.classHasFiberDeg_zeroClass :
475	    DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg (π := π) 0 (DivFunctor.zeroClass π T) :=
476	  DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_zero π T
477	
478	/-- **The degree-`0` slice `Div⁰_{X/S}(T)` is inhabited**, for every `π` and every
479	test object.
480	
481	This is the statement that turns the whole degree apparatus of `Picard/DivDegree.lean`
482	from vacuous into tested. Note what it is *not*: an identification of the slice with a
483	point. See the file docstring — singleton-ness at every test object is what
484	representability by the terminal object would need, and that is open. -/
485	noncomputable def DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass : (DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
486	  ⟨DivFunctor.zeroClass π T, DivFunctor.classHasFiberDeg_zeroClass π T⟩
487	
488	instance DivFunctorDeg.instNonemptyObjZero :
489	    Nonempty ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (Opposite.op T)) :=
490	  ⟨DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass π T⟩
491	
492	end Scheme
493	
494	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivFamilyZero
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FGAPicRepresentability
8	
9	/-!
10	# The Abel map at the empty divisor
11	
12	`Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean` supplies the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily`. This
13	file spends it on the one place where having an inhabitant changes what can be
14	*checked* rather than merely stated: the **Abel map**
15	
16	  `A_{C/k} : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`,  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[I_D]`.
17	
18	`Scheme.PicScheme.abelMap_app_mk` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`) states the
19	defining property `A([D]) = -[ker q]` for an arbitrary family. Before this file that
20	equation had **no instantiation**: `DivFamily` had no producer, so no value of the Abel
21	map was ever computed, and "the Abel map sends divisors to their line bundles" was a
22	statement about an empty domain.
23	
24	## What is proved
25	
26	`abelMap_zero`: `A([∅]) = 0`, i.e. the empty divisor goes to the **identity** of the
27	relative Picard group. Kleiman §3: `O(∅) = O`, so this is the normalisation an Abel map
28	must satisfy, and it is the first computed value of `abelMap` in the project.
29	
30	The proof is where the empty divisor's arithmetic shows up. `ker (0 : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0)` is
31	`O_{X_T}` (`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`, composed with
32	`Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso` because `DivFamily.q`'s source is stated as the
33	*pulled-back* unit). The zero of `PicSharp.relPresheaf` is *by definition* the class of
34	the unit line bundle (`RelPicFunctor.addCommGroup_via_tensorObj`), so the ideal class
35	is the group identity, and `neg_zero` finishes.
36	
37	## What this is not
38	
39	It is not a step of the seam: `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` is untouched, and no
40	antecedent of it is witnessed. It also does **not** discharge
41	`IdentityComponent.ClassDegreePinned`'s acceptance test
42	(`classDegree_ne_zero_of_exists_pos_fiberDeg`), which needs a divisor family of
43	degree `d ≠ 0` — the empty divisor has degree `0`, so it is exactly the family that
44	test cannot use. That producer is still owed, and it needs a rational point.
45	
46	What it does buy: the Abel map's defining equation, and the degree ledger of
47	`Picard/DivDegree.lean`, now have a worked instance to be wrong about. `abelDeg_zero`
48	below records the same value through the degree-refined Abel map, which is the form the
49	campaign's D-cluster consumes.
50	-/
51	
52	set_option autoImplicit false
53	
54	universe u
55	
56	open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry TopologicalSpace
57	
58	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
59	
60	namespace Scheme
61	
62	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
63	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
64	
65	/-- **The ideal sheaf of the empty divisor is the structure sheaf**, as a class in the
66	relative Picard group: `[I_∅] = [O] = 0`.
67	
68	`ker (0 : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0) ≅ O_{X_T}` by `kernelZeroIsoSource`, then
69	`Modules.pullbackUnitIso` identifies `DivFamily.q`'s pulled-back-unit source with the
70	structure sheaf, and the zero of `relPresheaf` *is* the unit class. -/
71	theorem PicSharp.kernelClass_divFamilyZero (T : (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
72	    (Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
73	      (⟨kernel (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop).q,
74	        (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop).kerLocallyTrivial⟩ :
75	        LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom))
76	      = (0 : (PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T) :=
77	  Quotient.sound (PicSharp.relPicRel_of_iso
78	    ⟨Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource ≪≫ Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso _⟩)
79	
80	variable [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
81	
82	/-- **THE ABEL MAP SENDS THE EMPTY DIVISOR TO THE IDENTITY**: `A([∅]) = 0`.
83	
84	`O(∅) = O` (Kleiman §3), the normalisation any Abel map must satisfy — and the **first
85	computed value of `abelMap` in this project**, since `DivFamily` had no inhabitant to
86	evaluate it at before `Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean`.
87	
88	Stated against `abelMapWitness`'s instance, i.e. via `abelMap_app_mk`, not under an
89	arbitrary `[HasAbelMap C]` binder — that class is a data slot inhabited by the constant
90	zero map, for which `abelMap_app_mk` provably fails (see its docstring, `I-0953`). Under
91	*that* inhabitant this equation would hold trivially and say nothing, which is exactly
92	why the instance matters here. -/
93	theorem PicScheme.abelMap_zero (T : (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
94	    (PicScheme.abelMap C).app T
95	        (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid C.hom T.unop) (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop))
96	      = (0 : (PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T) := by
97	  rw [PicScheme.abelMap_app_mk, PicSharp.kernelClass_divFamilyZero]
98	  exact neg_zero (G := ((PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T : Type _))
99	
100	/-- **The degree-refined Abel map at the empty divisor**, in the form the campaign's
101	D-cluster consumes: `A⁰([∅]) = 0`.
102	
103	`abelDeg C 0` is `divFunctorDegι ≫ abelMapWitness`, so this is `abelMap_zero` transported
104	along the degree-`0` inclusion; `abelDeg_app_mk` supplies the transport. -/
105	theorem PicScheme.abelDeg_zero (T : (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
106	    (PicScheme.abelDeg C 0).app T (DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass C.hom T.unop)
107	      = (0 : (PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T) := by
108	  rw [show (DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass C.hom T.unop) =
109	      ⟨Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid C.hom T.unop) (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop),
110	        DivFunctor.classHasFiberDeg_zeroClass C.hom T.unop⟩ from rfl,
111	    PicScheme.abelDeg_app_mk]
112	  exact PicScheme.abelMap_zero C T
113	
114	end Scheme
115	
116	end AlgebraicGeometry

768:structure DivFamily (π : X ⟶ S) (T : Over S) : Type (u + 1) where
769-  /-- The structure sheaf `O_D` of the divisor, as a quotient module on the
770-  relative product `X ×_S T`. -/
771-  F : (Limits.pullback π T.hom).Modules
772-  /-- `F` is finitely presented (automatic for an invertible ideal's
773-  quotient; kept to match the Quot-family shape). -/
774-  isFinitePresentation : F.IsFinitePresentation
775-  /-- `F = O_D` is flat over `T` — the divisor is a *relative* effective
776-  divisor (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:red`). -/
777-  flat : CoherentSheafFlat (pullback.snd π T.hom) F
778-  /-- The schematic support (the divisor `D` itself) is proper over `T`
779-  (automatic when `π` is proper; kept to match the Quot-family shape). -/
780-  properSupport : Modules.HasProperSupport (pullback.snd π T.hom) F
781-  /-- The quotient map `O_{X_T} ⟶ O_D` (source stated as the pulled-back
782-  unit, as in `QuotFamily` with `E = O_X`). -/
783-  q : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj
784-      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) ⟶ F
785-  /-- The quotient map is an epimorphism. -/
786-  epi : Epi q
787-  /-- **The divisor condition** (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:red`): the kernel ideal
788-  `I = ker q` is invertible, i.e. locally trivial of rank one. -/
789-  kerLocallyTrivial : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (Limits.kernel q)
790-
791-namespace DivFamily
792-
793-variable {π : X ⟶ S}
794-
795-/-- Two families of divisors are **equivalent** when an isomorphism of the
796-target sheaves commutes with the quotient maps — equivalently, when
797-`ker q = ker q'` as subobjects of `O_{X_T}`, i.e. when they cut out the same
798-closed subscheme (same convention as `QuotFamily.Rel`). -/
799-def Rel {T : Over S} (x y : DivFamily π T) : Prop :=
800-  ∃ f : x.F ≅ y.F, x.q ≫ f.hom = y.q
801-
802-lemma rel_refl {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T) : x.Rel x :=
803-  ⟨Iso.refl _, Category.comp_id _⟩
804-
805-lemma rel_symm {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y) : y.Rel x := by
806-  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
807-  exact ⟨f.symm, by rw [Iso.symm_hom, Iso.comp_inv_eq]; exact hf.symm⟩
808-
809-lemma rel_trans {T : Over S} {x y z : DivFamily π T}
810-    (h1 : x.Rel y) (h2 : y.Rel z) : x.Rel z := by
811-  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h1; obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := h2
812-  exact ⟨f ≪≫ g,
813-    (congrArg (x.q ≫ ·) (Iso.trans_hom f g)).trans <|
814-      (Category.assoc x.q f.hom g.hom).symm.trans <|
815-        (congrArg (· ≫ g.hom) hf).trans hg⟩
816-
817-/-- The equivalence-of-families setoid. -/
818-instance setoid (π : X ⟶ S) (T : Over S) : Setoid (DivFamily π T) where
819-  r := Rel
820-  iseqv := ⟨rel_refl, rel_symm, rel_trans⟩
821-
822-/-- The **pullback action** on a family of divisors along `ψ : T' ⟶ T` of
823-`Over S`: pull the sheaf and the quotient map back along
824-`quotBaseMap π ψ : X_{T'} ⟶ X_T`, matching the `O`-side through
825-`pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)` — exactly
826-`QuotFamily.pullbackAlong` at `E = O_X`.  The divisor condition base-changes
827-by `Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial`
828-(`lem:relative_divisor_base_change`). -/
829-noncomputable def pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T)
830-    (x : DivFamily π T) : DivFamily π T' where
831-  F := (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).obj x.F
832-  isFinitePresentation :=
833-    Modules.pullback_isFinitePresentation _ x.F x.isFinitePresentation
834-  flat := fun {_} hU {_} hV e =>
835-    CoherentSheafFlat.of_isPullback (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.F
836-      (letI := x.isFinitePresentation; inferInstance) x.flat hU hV e
837-  properSupport :=
838-    Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.F
839-      x.isFinitePresentation x.properSupport
840-  q := (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
841-      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv ≫
842-    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q
843-  epi :=
844-    @CategoryTheory.epi_comp _ _ _ _ _
845-      (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
846-        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv inferInstance
847-      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q)
848-      (@CategoryTheory.Functor.map_epi _ _ _ _

abelian); naturality is `map_neg` of the group-homomorphism pullback maps of
`Pic^♯` (`PicSharp.relFunctorial`).  Building the negation at the
`AddCommGrpCat`-valued level (rather than on the forgotten set-valued
`picSharp`) keeps the group structure directly available — the forget-composite
`(picSharp C).obj T` does not expose its `AddGroup` to instance search. -/
noncomputable def relPresheafNeg {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ PicSharp.relPresheaf C where
  app T := AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (-AddMonoidHom.id _)
  naturality {T T'} g := by
    ext a
    exact (map_neg (PicSharp.relFunctorial C.hom T.unop.hom T'.unop.hom
      g.unop.left (Over.w g.unop).symm) a).symm

/-- **Negation on the relative Picard functor**, as a natural transformation
`Pic^♯_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`.  Pointwise it is `a ↦ -a` in the group
`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`; it is the set-valued shadow (`whiskerRight … (forget _)`) of
the group-presheaf negation `relPresheafNeg`, so its naturality is inherited
for free. -/
noncomputable def picNeg {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    picSharp C ⟶ picSharp C :=
  Functor.whiskerRight (relPresheafNeg C) (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})

/-- **The Abel map witness** `A_{C/k} : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`,
`[D] ↦ [O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[ker q]`, the substantive natural transformation
underlying the line-bundle / Quot correspondence (Kleiman §3 Def. `dfn:Abel`).
Assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`. -/
noncomputable def abelMapWitness {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    divFunctor C ⟶ picSharp C :=
  abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C

/-- Class **carrying the Abel map** `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`.  It is a
data-carrying class with field `abel`; the instance `instHasAbelMap` supplies
the witness `abelMapWitness C`.

**PROPERTY-FREE DATA SLOT — corrected 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`, from a
fresh-context vacuity sweep). The previous text claimed that `abelMap :=
HasAbelMap.abel` "inherits the concrete construction and the defining property
`abelMap_app_mk`". Both halves are false under the class binder**, and the
second is provably so.

The single field constrains nothing beyond the *type* of `abel`. Machine-checked:
the constant-zero transformation inhabits the class — its naturality is
`map_zero` of the pullback group hom, so it is free — and under that instance
`abelMap C` is identically `0`, sending every divisor class to `0`. Probing
`abelMap_app_mk`'s conclusion against it, `rfl` **fails**. So `abelMap_app_mk`
is a statement about `instHasAbelMap` alone, never about the class: a consumer
quantifying over `[HasAbelMap C]` gets an arbitrary natural transformation with
no Abel-map content. This is the `ClassDegree` collapse
(`IdentityComponent.lean:1450-1461`) one level up, and it is the
property-free-data-field sibling of the `HasDivFunctor` vacuity recorded in this
file's §2 caveat.

Blast radius is small at HEAD and this is a documentation fix, not a repair: the

use `abelMapWitness`; the alternative is to add the pin as a field, as

class HasAbelMap {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] where
  /-- The Abel map itself (data). -/
  abel : divFunctor C ⟶ picSharp C

/-- The **Abel map** `A_{C/k} : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, sending a relative
effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` to its associated invertible
sheaf `[O_{C ×_k T}(D)] = [I_D⁻¹]`.

**Not under an arbitrary `[HasAbelMap C]` binder** — that class is a

`abelMap_app_mk` provably fails there (see the class docstring, and `I-0953`).

    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]

the identity `(annihilator F).ideal U = Ann_{Γ(X,U)}(Γ(F,U))` is the downstream
characterization lemma (`annihilator_ideal`, blocked on the QCoh localization bridge).

This is a project-local primitive: Mathlib does not carry an annihilator ideal sheaf
for sheaves of modules on a scheme. -/
noncomputable def annihilator (F : X.Modules) : X.IdealSheafData :=
  IdealSheafData.ofIdeals fun U => Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1)

/-- The component of the annihilator ideal sheaf at an affine open is contained in the
module annihilator of the sections. This is the always-available (`ofIdeals`) direction
of the characterization; the reverse inclusion is the basic-open coherence blocked on
`isLocalizedModule_basicOpen`. Project-local because `annihilator` is. -/
lemma annihilator_ideal_le (F : X.Modules) (U : X.affineOpens) :
    (annihilator F).ideal U ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1) :=
  IdealSheafData.ideal_ofIdeals_le _ _

/-- The **schematic support** of a sheaf of modules `F` on a scheme `X`
(`def:schematic_support`): the closed subscheme of `X` cut out by the annihilator
ideal sheaf `annihilator F`. Project-local because `annihilator` is. -/
noncomputable def schematicSupport (F : X.Modules) : Scheme.{u} :=
  (annihilator F).subscheme

/-- The canonical closed immersion of the schematic support into the ambient scheme,
realizing `schematicSupport F` as a closed subscheme of `X` (`def:schematic_support`).
This is the `IdealSheafData.subschemeι` of the annihilator ideal sheaf; it is a
`IsPreimmersion` + `QuasiCompact` immersion onto the support. Project-local because
`annihilator` is. -/
noncomputable def schematicSupportι (F : X.Modules) : schematicSupport F ⟶ X :=
  (annihilator F).subschemeι

/-- The sheaf of modules `F` **has proper support over `S` along `f`**
(`def:has_proper_support`): the composite of the schematic-support immersion with
`f : X ⟶ S` is a proper morphism. Since `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper` is stable under
base change, this condition is preserved by pullback, as required by the Quot functor's
pullback action. Project-local because `schematicSupport` is. -/
def HasProperSupport {S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) : Prop :=
  IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f)

end Scheme.Modules
